name: Fox

app.note: The scale is 1.5504 m for each unit: 1.3 times the scale that puts the standing head top of the fox at 1.083 m, the head top of the parametric fox (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-mesh/landmark-probe.txt and scale-variants.txt), because the user asked for a fox 1.3 times the size on 2026-10-14 (docs/research/2026-10-14-animal-size.md). The leg factor raises the standing shoulder joint from 0.625 to 0.715 units, so app.shoulders is 1.108536 m, and the scale stays, so that the trunk, the head before its factor, and the arms keep their meters (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-form.md). The user asked for a full violin on 2026-10-14 ("fox and rabbit violin too small"), and the arms reached 0.6036 m (docs/research/2026-10-14-neck-violin.md). Then the user asked for shorter arms with the same violin ("reduce the arm length of the fox and rabbit without changing the violin size"). Of the reaches 0.4901 m, 0.5452 m, and 0.6036 m, the manager chose the middle one, so the reach is 0.5452 m, and the violin stays 0.998 of the violin of the app (docs/research/2026-10-14-arms-rest.md).

armFactorNote: The factor of the upper arm and the forearm that gives the reach of app.reach from the joints below at the scale of app.shoulders. pnpm rig-mesh fox --check measured 0.4574 m with no factor at this scale. The factor was 1.0782 before the full violin and 1.35 with it, and the middle factor 1.21 shortens the arms that the user found too long (docs/research/2026-10-14-arms-rest.md). With no --check, pnpm rig-mesh stops when the reach is more than 1% from app.reach.
legFactorNote: The factor of the thigh and the shin. Each one stretches only between its joints, the foot keeps its size, and the body rises 0.09 units, so that the soles stay at y 0. The user asked for longer legs and a higher seat on 2026-10-14, and then said that the legs of the factor 2.0 were too long. The legs give a seat of 0.235 m (0.164 m before), and the chair of the app is 0.36 m high (seat of ANIMALS), so the feet hang. The factor 3.25 gave the seat of the reference fox, about one visible head (0.484 m), with a standing fox of 2.23 m (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-form.md).
headFactorNote: The factor of the head and the ears around the neck joint. The weights blend the growth over the neck. The user asked for a larger head that appears cuter on 2026-10-14, and then said that the head of the factor 1.5 was too big. With 1.25, a thin face between the neck and the head turned over when the head turned, and the fox folded in 15.0% of the play samples. The factors 1.2 and 1.3 gave 3.3% and 6.5% (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-form/rig-mesh-check-fox-head-variants.log). The export keeps the head height and the head center of the head before the factor for the holds (ungrown() of tools/studio-body.ts).
neckFactorNote: The factor of the length of the neck between the neck joint and the head joint. The neck shortens only between its joints, and the head and the ears keep their size and move down the neck with the head joint. The export moves the head center of the holds with the head (headRig() of tools/studio-body.ts). The user said "fox neck too long" on 2026-10-14. Of the factors 0.8, 0.65, and 0.5 (the head 2.2, 3.9, and 5.6 cm down), the manager chose the middle one (docs/research/2026-10-14-neck-violin.md).
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the pose of the source: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tips, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The probes are in docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-mesh/. sections.py gives the cuts at each height: the feet below y 0.05 (the toes forward to z 0.14), the thin shins from 0.05 to 0.11, the wide thighs from 0.13 to the crotch at 0.23, the body from 0.23 to 0.51 (x ±0.093 under the arms), the shoulders at 0.53 to 0.66, the narrow neck at 0.69 to 0.71 (x ±0.089), the head from 0.71 with the muzzle to z 0.28, and the ears apart from 0.91. The trunk joints lie 0.01 to 0.02 behind the middle of the body cut, as in the rabbit, from the hips over the crotch to the chest 0.085 below the shoulder joint. The thigh joint lies at the crotch on the middle of the leg cut, the knee where the thin shin meets the wide thigh, the ankle where the foot starts, and the toes at the ball of the foot. The ear joint lies on the line of the middles of the ear cuts at 0.91 and 0.95, at the top of the head (0.89), and its tail at the ear tip. The cuts at x 0.101 to 0.221 give the middle line of the free arm (sections-x.txt), which leaves the body between x 0.081 and 0.101. The shoulder joint lies on that line, 0.03 inside the root (x 0.07). The wrist lies at the narrow cut where the paw starts (arm-axis.txt, s 0.01 to 0.02), the elbow halfway from the shoulder joint to the wrist and 0.01 behind the line, and the finger joint at the knuckles, 0.03 before the tip of the paw. The tail is a chain of two bones (tail_line.py, tail-line.txt). The tail joint lies at the middle of the root of the tail, between its top on the back (y 0.42, z -0.09) and its bottom on the thighs (y 0.26, z -0.055). The tail_tip joint lies at the bend of the middle line of the tail cuts, where the tail leaves the body (y 0.25, z -0.15), 0.117 units from the root, and its tail at the tip of the tail (y 0.01, z -0.247). Each roll is the hint of the z axis of the bone, forward by default. The arm bones take the normal of the palm (palm): the smallest principal direction of the vertices of the left paw, inward and back (facts.txt).

studio.note: The studio has no fox. The seat is the seat of a long thigh: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind pose to the source, and the right side mirrors it. The thigh lies level on the seat, 8 degrees out, so that the haunch and the back of the thigh rest on the seat (the user saw the fox sitting on the edge of the chair on 2026-10-14), and the shin keeps the turn of the source, so that it hangs under the knee. With 15 degrees below the level, the haunch perched above the back of the seat. The foot and the toes turn 20 degrees further down than in the source, as relaxed feet that hang above the floor (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-form/leg_turns.py). The seat of the studio rabbit turned the thigh 57 degrees, and the long thigh of the fox stood almost upright on the chair. The bind arms are the bind arms of the studio rabbit (tools/mesh-rigs/rabbit.json, docs/research/2026-10-13-rabbit-mesh/studio-targets.ts): the unit direction of each left arm bone in the bind pose. tailBind gives the direction of each tail bone in the seated bind pose: the root goes back over the seat, 7 degrees below the level, and the tip hangs back and down behind the chair, 54 degrees below the level. Then the tail goes at most 0.0005 units over the seat top, and its lowest point is 0.037 units above the soles.

weights.stretchRampNote: With a ramp, the upper arm stretches by the arm factor only on the free arm: the share of the stretch fades from 0 to 1 over this many units on each side of the plane |x| = armSplit. 0 gives no ramp. With the arm factor 1.35 and the hold of the neck round, the ramp of 0.02 folded the faces of the trunk below the right armpit in 20.9% of the play samples, and 29.7% with no ramp (docs/research/2026-10-14-neck-violin.md). With the later holds, the ramp folds more: with the hold of main, 14.2% against 9.9% with no ramp (docs/research/2026-10-14-rig-retro.md), and with the arm factor 1.21 and the fitted hold, 15.7% against 12.8% (docs/research/2026-10-14-arms-rest/rig-mesh-check-fox-ramp.log). The rabbit has no ramp either.

sliver.note: The corners of each thin face share one set of weights, so that the face moves rigidly and does not turn over at a bent joint. A thin face has a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge below longest (units). The values are the values of the rabbit.

line.note: The middle corner of each long thin face (a corner angle above angle, in degrees) takes the mix of the weights of its two other corners by its place along their line, so that it does not lag behind the line when a joint bends. With head, the corners of the head take the rule too. A thin face of the jaw (corner angle 172 degrees, 5 cm long) and a thin face under the chin (153 degrees) folded in 35% and 9% of the play samples when the head turned against the neck, and with this rule in none (pnpm fold-probe fox-violinist).

weights.clavicleFromNote: The share of the clavicle weight that a vertex keeps grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height (units), and the chest takes the rest. Bone heat gave a small face of the right chest (y 0.57) a clavicle weight of 0.07 on one corner and the spine on the others. The bow arm turns the right clavicle far, so the face turned over in 76% of the play samples. The clavicle joint is at y 0.635.
weights.armTopNote: The share of the weight of the clavicles and of the upper arms that a vertex keeps falls from 1 at the lower height to 0 at the upper height (units), and the neck takes the rest. The shoulders end at y 0.66 and the neck is narrowest at 0.69 to 0.71. Bone heat gave a vertex of the side of the neck 0.33 of the right clavicle and 0.24 of the right upper arm, and a raised bow arm dragged them.
weights.shoulderHeadNote: Below headFrom, the share of the head weight that goes to the neck grows from 0 at the smaller distance from the middle plane to all at the larger distance (units). The values are the values of the rabbit, scaled by the neck of the fox (x ±0.089 against ±0.077).
weights.fingersNote: The fingers keep this share of their bone heat weight, and the hand takes the rest, as in the rabbit.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the buttocks stay on the hips and the long thigh turns onto the seat. With the ramp of the first config (0.11 to 0.185), the upper half of the thigh stayed upright. With the ramp from 0.2 to 0.27, 9 faces of the hip crease turned over in the seated bind, and with this ramp none.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones: the cuts of sections.py x show the arm apart from the body from x 0.101 out. Above headFrom, each vertex except the ears follows the head only: the neck is narrowest at y 0.69 to 0.71, and the cheek fur starts at 0.73. Each ear vertex goes to its ear bone with a ramp over the heights of earBase. The tail has two bones (tail): the vertices within radius of the line from the root over the bend to the tip, and behind the plane z = behind, follow the tail bones. The share of the tail bones grows from 0 to 1 over the places of root along the line (units from the root), the share of the tip within the tail grows from 0 to 1 over bend units on each side of the bend, and the share of the tail bones takes the mean of its neighbors in smooth rounds, so that the root has no hard edge. The radius holds the widest cut of the tail (x Â±0.103 at y 0.21), and the plane keeps the backs of the thighs (z -0.04 at y 0.21) out of it.

refine.ringsNote: The first config has no rings. pnpm rig-mesh fox --check lists the thin faces near the joints as candidates for a ring (check.thin).

flip.note: The long edge of a face of the arms with a corner angle above angle (degrees) in the seated bind mesh flips to the corner of the face on its other side, when the two faces lie almost on one plane (normals, degrees) and the surface moves at most move (units). The values are the values of the rabbit.

check.note: pnpm rig-mesh --check lists the faces of the seated bind mesh with a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge of at least length (units), when that edge passes within near (units) of a joint of the arms or the legs. These faces are candidates for a ring (refine.rings). The values are the values of the rabbit.

colors.note: Each face takes the mean sRGB color of the texture at the samples of a grid of the given steps on the face. A face is dark when its share of samples with a linear luminance below dark is at least eyeShare, and then it takes the mean of its dark samples. Each other face takes the mean of its samples that are not dark. A dark face in the eye box (the left eye at x 0.043, y 0.805 in the front view, mirrored for the right eye) is a face of an eye. A face in the nose box whose color is nearer to the nose color than to white is a face of the nose: the nose of the fox is black, at the tip of the muzzle (y 0.765, z 0.28). The box starts above the dark faces of the mouth (y 0.736 to 0.75), which the first box held. Then each face takes the nearest color of a palette of palette colors, from k-means in Oklab.

eyeShell.note: Each eye shell is a fan from the middle of the dark faces of the eye to at most this number of points of their edge, lifted this far (units) along the normal of the eye. The values are the values of the rabbit.

chair.note: The chair is wider than the chair of the rabbit rig, because the haunch of the fox is x ±0.17. Its front edge lies behind the heels of the seated bind (z 0.155 with the leg factor), so that the long thighs lie on the seat. The seat top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail.

sit.note: The underside of the haunch behind the hip joints goes down onto the seat in the seated bind (sit() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), because the buttocks of the mesh curve up behind the hip joints. The manager found the back of the haunch 3 to 11 cm above the seat on 2026-10-14. The drop of each vertical line over the seat is its gap less gap, at most most, and it fades over ramp units before the hip joints and over the last end units of the haunch. The drops take the mean of their neighbors in smooth rounds on a grid of step units, and each vertex moves by the drop less its height above the underside, to 0 at band units. The side view of the underside is 10.5 cm above the seat at most before, and 1.4 cm after. With a band of 0.1 units, a face of the right side of the haunch turned over (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-fix.md). The corrective shapes give the source back, so the standing body keeps its form.

smooth.note: The fur spikes at the bottom of the back of the head hang over the back of the neck, and with the head factor 1.2 and the neck factor 0.65 they made a dark jagged band under the head from the back and the sides (the manager on 2026-10-14). The band shows also with the factors 1 (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-fix.md), so the rig smooths the source inside the box before the growth: the back of the neck and the bottom of the back of the head (x from -0.11 to 0.11, y from 0.66 to 0.78, behind z 0.03). The muzzle, the jaw, the eyes, the cheek fur at the sides, and the ears stay outside the box. Each vertex inside moves 0.5 of the way to the middle of its neighbors in 12 rounds, at most 0.035 units.
